description: Say something to a conversation while it is running a turn. **This tool blocks until the new turn ends** (it moves to the background only when timeout_ms expires). Two modes: interject (default) stops the current turn and redirects at once; queue does not stop it and speaks right after the current turn ends naturally (without using the dsh_queue queue). To stop without saying anything use dsh_interrupt; to run after the current turn without blocking use dsh_send(queue=true). On an idle conversation it runs as **an ordinary wait=true turn** (full result, not a receipt). Note: ACP refuses concurrent prompts, so steering the model inside the same turn is not possible; interject is the practical equivalent (cancel, then start a new turn immediately, with history intact).

client_run_id.description: Caller-generated idempotency key (up to 128 characters, scoped to this conversation). Submitting it again returns the first run instead of interjecting twice.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id, from dsh_start or dsh_list.

mode.description: interject (default) = stop and redirect; queue = speak after the current turn finishes.

reasoning.description: How much reasoning to return. Default hide.

review.description: Review policy for this turn, overriding the conversation default (advisory); off skips the review ticket this time.

timeout_ms.description: Upper bound on **waiting** for the new turn, in milliseconds. **Default 0 = wait forever**; in queue mode it also bounds the wait for the previous turn to end. While busy, a wait that times out is an error (the message was not sent and the conversation is unharmed); when idle, expiry only moves the turn to the background without cancelling it.

name: dsh_interject
title: Interject
